sections.h2: Which office bills property tax in Pearland
sections.html:
Your parcel's county decides. Pearland spreads across Brazoria County and Fort Bend County, and the City of Pearland is an active taxing unit in both appraisal districts.

  • Brazoria County tax office, 451 N. Velasco St., Angleton, 979-864-1320. It collects for the City of Pearland and Pearland ISD.
  • Brazoria Central Appraisal District (values), 500 N. Chenango St., Angleton, 979-849-7792.
  • Fort Bend Central Appraisal District (values), 2801 B.F. Terry Blvd., Rosenberg, 281-344-8623.

For a Fort Bend County address, ask the Fort Bend County tax office where your bill is paid.

Expect more than the city and school lines on a bill. Brazoria County parcels may carry Pearland Municipal Management District #2, Alvin Community College District, emergency districts, drainage districts and dozens of numbered municipal utility districts. A newer subdivision often has a utility district charge that an older one lacks.

The school line varies too. Pearland ISD, Alvin ISD and Friendswood ISD all serve parts of the county, so the school charge on your own bill shows which district covers your street.

The City of Pearland's 2026 notice shows $0.637892 as the no-new-revenue rate and $0.693542 as the voter-approval rate, both per $100 of value. The lower figure would raise the same total as last year from property taxed in both years. The higher one is, in most cases, the most a city can adopt without calling an election.

For the rate actually set, check your bill or call Pearland's finance staff or the Brazoria County tax office. The full rate worksheet can be viewed at Pearland City Hall, 3519 Liberty Dr.

Every Texas taxing unit follows one statewide calendar anchored on New Year's Day. On that date both the property's value and its owner are fixed for the year.

  • January 1: value is set, and that year's lien takes hold.
  • April 1 or soon after: notices of appraised value start going to single-family homesteads, with other property following near May 1.
  • Before May 1: apply for most exemptions.
  • May 15, or thirty days after delivery of the notice when that is later: protest deadline.
  • July 25: the appraisal roll is certified and sent to every taxing unit.
  • September 29 or thereabouts: last day for units to adopt rates.
  • October: bills are mailed. Tax is due by January 31 and delinquent February 1.

An account still open on the first of February is charged six percent penalty and one percent interest. After that the penalty grows monthly and reaches twelve percent on July 1, with interest still ticking up. Where a unit has hired a collection lawyer, a fee of as much as 20 percent can follow.

Protest hearings before the appraisal review board begin around May 15. The board is expected to approve the records by July 20 unless more than five percent of total value is still under protest. Save the envelope or delivery record for your appraisal notice, since a late delivery moves your protest deadline.

Apply for the homestead exemption the first year you live in the house as your main home. Pearland-area schools take $140,000 off value for the school tax, and owners 65 or older or disabled receive an extra $60,000. Cities and counties can adopt a percentage break as large as 20 percent of value (minimum $5,000), so ask Pearland whether it has.

Homesteads are protected from fast value jumps too. From the January after the first exemption, appraised value may rise no more than 10 percent annually. Seniors and disabled owners can also cap their school tax, and the cap follows them to a new Texas homestead.

A disabled veteran may exempt part of one property. The scale by VA disability rating runs like this:

  • Rating of 10 to 29 percent: a deduction as high as $5,000
  • Rating of 30 to 49 percent: as high as $7,500
  • Rating of 50 to 69 percent: as high as $10,000
  • Rating of 70 to 100 percent: as high as $12,000

A 100 percent rating makes the residence homestead fully exempt. An heir to a Pearland house who is on no recorded deed may still apply, with an ownership affidavit, the death certificate, a recent utility bill and any court record citation handed to the appraisal district.

sections.h2: Selling a Pearland house with unpaid taxes
sections.html:
Back tax follows the lot, not the seller. A fresh lien starts every January 1 and delinquent amounts block clear title for a buyer. Even after a sale, the person who owned the house on that date can be sued over that year's bill.

Late charges can often be waived. Pay the tax by the 21st day after you learn it was delinquent and get a written request in before day 181. A residence homestead owner can ask for a payment plan, and some collectors allow 36 months. While an appraisal appeal is pending, keep the undisputed amount current before the delinquency date.

If a lawsuit ends in a sale, a former homestead owner can buy back within two years of the purchaser's deed filing, and other land within 180 days. Surplus proceeds stay claimable by the former owner for two years.

Gather these before you list: your latest bill from the county that holds the parcel, any exemption confirmation, and a note of which school district serves the address. A buyer's agent will ask about utility district charges, so find out whether your neighborhood has one.

The sequence is short. Get a written payoff from the county holding your parcel, pass it to the title company, and let closing clear the older years first. Then work out with the buyer how this year is divided.

A split payment works for any owner: one half by the end of November, the rest by the end of June. Seniors and disabled homestead owners get four installments instead. If you are selling, talk to the tax office before starting a plan, because whatever remains is cleared at closing.

The city grew from 91,252 residents in 2010 to 125,828 in 2020, with 129,930 estimated for July 2025. About 76.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied, a typical one is worth $356,300, and median household income is $118,842.

faqs.q: Is Pearland in Brazoria County or Fort Bend County?
faqs.a: Both. The city is a taxing unit in each appraisal district, and where your parcel sits determines which one appraises it.

faqs.q: When is Pearland property tax delinquent?
faqs.a: Anything unpaid after January 31 becomes delinquent on February 1, when penalty and interest begin. By July 1 the penalty stands at twelve percent.

faqs.q: What rate does Pearland charge for 2026?
faqs.a: The 2026 notice shows two benchmark figures, $0.637892 and $0.693542. Your bill or the city finance office shows the rate actually set.

faqs.q: Can I pay Pearland property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. Half can be paid by the end of November and half by the end of June, and older or disabled homestead owners can use four installments. A homestead owner who is behind may ask for a plan up to 36 months long.

faqs.q: Who owes the current year's tax after a Pearland sale?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner carries the legal liability. At closing the year is normally prorated, and older delinquent years are paid out of the proceeds.
